title: Bitcoin Slides Into “Deep Value Zone” as BTC Prices Continue Declining on Saturday – CoinDesk
body:
Bitcoin’s price slipped further on Saturday, sinking below the $64,000 mark and carving out what analysts are calling a “deep‑value zone.” The cryptocurrency has lost roughly 7 % since the close of U.S. equity markets on Friday, extending a multi‑day downtrend that has seen a string of red candles dominate the charts. Traders who missed the rally three months ago are now watching the market sell at levels they once hoped to capture, a sentiment echoed by market commentator James Check.

The latest dip brings Bitcoin’s price to about $63,905, a level that sits well beneath the recent support range of $68,000‑$70,000 that held steady through much of the spring. Technical indicators point to increasing bearish momentum: the 50‑day moving average has crossed below the 200‑day line, forming a classic “death cross,” while the Relative Strength Index (RSI) has slipped into the 30‑35 band, suggesting the asset is approaching oversold territory. Yet, the sheer volume of sell orders—particularly from large‑scale holders liquidating positions—signals that the market may be testing the depth of demand rather than simply correcting a short‑term overextension.

Fundamental factors are also weighing on sentiment. The broader crypto ecosystem has been grappling with regulatory uncertainty, especially after recent statements from U.S. authorities hinting at stricter oversight of digital asset exchanges and stablecoins. Meanwhile, macroeconomic pressures persist: higher‑for‑longer interest rates, lingering inflation concerns, and a resilient U.S. dollar have all contributed to a risk‑off environment that traditionally disfavors speculative assets like Bitcoin. The cryptocurrency’s correlation with equity markets has re‑emerged, as the S&P 500’s modest gains on Friday failed to lift Bitcoin, underscoring a decoupling that many investors find unsettling.

Despite the gloom, some market participants view the current price level as a potential entry point. The “deep‑value zone” terminology reflects a belief that Bitcoin is being undervalued relative to its long‑term fundamentals, such as its scarcity (capped at 21 million coins) and growing institutional adoption. Several large asset managers have recently disclosed modest allocations to the digital asset, and a handful of major corporations continue to hold Bitcoin on their balance sheets, providing a floor of demand that could stabilize the market if confidence returns. Moreover, upcoming events—most notably the anticipated halving in 2024, which historically precedes bullish cycles—remain on investors’ radar, potentially fueling speculative buying ahead of the supply shock.

Nevertheless, short‑term risks remain pronounced. The market’s liquidity is thin compared with traditional assets, making price swings more abrupt. Any further negative regulatory news, such as enforcement actions against major exchanges, could trigger a cascade of stop‑loss orders, driving the price deeper into the $60,000 range. Additionally, the crypto‑specific “hashrate” metric, which measures the computational power securing the Bitcoin network, has shown a slight decline in recent weeks, hinting at miner unease that could translate into reduced network security and further price pressure.

Looking ahead, Bitcoin’s trajectory will likely hinge on a confluence of technical rebounds, regulatory clarity, and macroeconomic developments. If the price can hold above the $60,000 threshold and attract renewed buying interest, the next few weeks could see a modest recovery toward the $68,000 support zone. Conversely, a breach of that level may open the door to a more extended correction, potentially testing the $55,000 mark. Investors and observers will be watching closely for any shift in market sentiment, as the cryptocurrency navigates a pivotal moment that could set the tone for the remainder of the year.
